clue.text: Run rule over American big beast

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the run-and-rule pair is read from the end backwards

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Someone laying down the law to a large American animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses both run and rule together, not just the rule; R is the cricket abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is a huge tusked marine mammal, easily a big beast.

clue.text: Stupid Spectator has lies for news, primarily

indicators.note: for marks a swap: one letter takes another's place

parts.note: a witness is an onlooker, a spectator

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of news, and of lies too

parts.note: primarily applies to lies as well, giving its first letter L

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Spectator magazine prints lies instead of news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the L of 'lies' in place of the N of 'news' in WITNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Witless means lacking wits or sense, hence foolish.

clue.text: Fat: apparently good to be inside a covering

indicators.note: to be inside means the next piece goes within the covering

parts.note: a lid is a covering
pi, short for pious, describes someone who seems virtuous

explanation.surface: Fat seemingly benefits from being wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, ostentatiously good.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the biochemical class of fats and oils.

clue.text: Stew spooned up without demur

indicators.note: to stew is to mix and cook, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stew spooned up without complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' rearranges SPOONED and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unopposed meets no resistance or objection.

clue.text: For sale (not united): can and mug

indicators.note: not says a letter for united is dropped from the phrase meaning for sale

parts.note: an item for sale is there to buy
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football club names
jug and can are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A shop label: an item for sale, then a can and a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not united' takes U out of TO BUY, leaving TOBY. A Toby jug is a drinking vessel shaped like a seated man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a pottery drinking vessel, a kind of mug moulded as a stout figure.

clue.text: Without note, go with the others to make speech to Filipinos

indicators.note: without says the letter for note is removed

parts.note: to tag along is to follow a group
N stands for note, as in a banknote

explanation.surface: Instructions to join the crowd so as to address people in the Philippines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without note' takes N out of TAG ALONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the principal language of the Philippines, the basis of Filipino.

clue.text: A Nazi group interrupts sexually ambivalent singers

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the inner piece goes inside

parts.note: bi is short for bisexual
the SS was a Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: Nazi thugs break in on a group of bisexual singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' puts the A and the Nazi SS inside 'bi'; 'A' is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassi is the Italian plural of basso, deep-voiced male vocalists.

clue.text: Most stylish relative I joke about

indicators.note: about means around, so the joke surrounds the rest

parts.note: a jest is a joke
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone joking about how stylish their relative is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the joke around the relative and I; 'joke' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means smart and stylish, so the superlative is the most rakish.

clue.text: Withdraw permission to pick up taxi after golf

indicators.note: after places the golf letter before the rest

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to pick up here means to collect, so the taxi goes inside

parts.note: OK is permission

indicators.note: up in a down clue reverses the taxi word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Revoking permission to collect a taxi after a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick' is containment and 'up' reverses the taxi in a down clue; 'after' puts golf first.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat or retract is to return whence one came, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Students keep a little storage in the cloud

indicators.note: keep means hold in, so the students surround the rest

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
a means one, the Roman numeral I
MB, a megabyte, is a small amount of computer storage

explanation.surface: Students keep a few files in cloud storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the UK's National Union of Students; 'in the cloud' plays on online storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain-bearing cloud, or a halo of light.

clue.text: Cautiously progressing petition about the end of hunting

indicators.note: about can mean scattered around, so these letters are rearranged
the end of picks the final letter of hunting

explanation.surface: A petition concerning the abolition of hunting with hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges PETITION with G, the last letter of 'hunting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on the balls of the feet is moving forward carefully and quietly.

clue.text: Silly argument over half a small pigeon

indicators.note: over half means more than half of the word for a silly argument is kept, from its start

parts.note: a squabble is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Two people bickering over a share of a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over half' means more than half: five of the eight letters of SQUABBLE are kept, not an exact half.
explanation.definitionFit: A squab is a young pigeon, still unfledged and small.

clue.text: Eventually find oneself in satire that's not succeeded

indicators.note: not says the letter for succeeded is dropped from the word for satire

parts.note: a send-up is a satirical parody
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone eventually lands in a satire that flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not succeeded' takes S off the front of SEND UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up somewhere is to arrive there at last, often by accident: a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: A missile may be basic; it'll go off

indicators.note: go off as in explode, so the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A warning that even a basic missile will explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' rearranges BASIC and ITLL; the definition is an adjective: a missile may be ballistic.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballistic missile follows a free-falling trajectory once its rocket burns out.

clue.text: On board ship are people with non-PC views

indicators.note: on board ship means placed inside the abbreviation for steamship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to exist is to be, so they are means they exist

explanation.surface: Politically incorrect people are aboard the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' puts EXIST inside SS, the steamship abbreviation that surrounds goods carried on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Those prejudiced by gender hold views counter to political correctness.

clue.text: Hammer this, or use axes to chop and polish

parts.note: graph axes are labelled x and y
to lop is to chop off
to hone is to sharpen or polish

explanation.surface: Instructions for a woodworker: strike it or use axes to cut and smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' are graph axes, X and Y, not tools; a xylophone is played with hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is struck with small mallets, so it is an instrument one hammers.

clue.text: Well woman visits teacher, missing a university

indicators.note: visits means goes into, so the woman is placed inside
missing says a letter for university is left out of the word for teacher

parts.note: a guru is a spiritual teacher
U is the abbreviation for university
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A healthy woman calls on a teacher, skipping university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops one U from the teacher; 'visits' puts the woman inside. 'Well' posing as an adjective hides the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is an oil well that spouts freely without pumping.

clue.text: Browsing the web, taken in by visionary poet

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the visionary word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or visionary
someone browsing the web is on the net

explanation.surface: A visionary poet duped while surfing the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts ON NET inside SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer is a writer of sonnets, so a poet.

clue.text: Boy left in empty gallery with delight

indicators.note: in places the boy and left inside what remains of the gallery
empty means hollowed, keeping only the outside letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy left alone in a deserted gallery, very pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of gallery; 'in' puts boy and left between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something happily and willingly is doing it with pleasure, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Securing boat, ready for Chinese peninsula

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the currency surrounds the boat

parts.note: ready is slang for cash; the yuan is China's currency
a cat is a catboat or catamaran

explanation.surface: Mooring a boat, prepared for a Chinese peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is cash, so 'ready for Chinese' is YUAN; 'Chinese' only qualifies the money, the peninsula being Mexican.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatán is a large peninsula in south-east Mexico.

clue.text: Means arranged one day for comeback

indicators.note: a comeback returns, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: set means arranged
taken as the word one

explanation.surface: A performer arranges a single date for a return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for comeback' reverses SET + ONE + D to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify something is to indicate or stand for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Buck up everyone in staff

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the whole construction backwards
in places everyone inside the staff

parts.note: a rod is a staff
all means everyone

explanation.surface: An exhortation to cheer up all the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places everyone inside the staff, then 'up' reverses the whole, as fits a down clue; 'Buck up' is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck is American slang for a dollar.

clue.text: Alcohol in pack, partly empty

parts.note: a scrum is formed by a rugby pack

indicators.note: empty means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Drink in a rucksack, part-consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUMPY is rough cider from the West of England; 'partly empty' gives PY, not part of 'empty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a strong, rough farmhouse cider, so a kind of alcohol.

clue.text: Danger: people shot in court

parts.note: men are people
an ace is an unreturned serve on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A shooting in a law court endangers people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' means a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat, something dangerous.

clue.text: Depending on results, group of countries to be reduced by one state

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: an empire is a group of countries under one ruler
one is the Roman numeral I, set by (beside) the shortened word
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Talk of an empire shrinking by one state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' clips the last letter off; 'by one' sets I beside it, and the state is California.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge rests on observation and experiment rather than theory.

clue.text: Bravo, smashing the basis for one threatening your job?

indicators.note: smashing into means breaking into, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a root is a basis or origin
B is bravo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Bravo for smashing the foundations of automation that endangers work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' puts B into ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Automation by machines is widely feared as a threat to human employment.

clue.text: Boy not force-fed fish

indicators.note: not says the letter for force is dropped from fed

parts.note: taken as the word fed
F is the physics symbol for force
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A boy who wasn't made to eat fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force-fed' reads as one word but splits: 'not force' strips F from 'fed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar is a male first name, so a boy in crossword terms.

clue.text: Serious about married brothers

indicators.note: about means around, so serious wraps the married letter

parts.note: grim means stern or serious

explanation.surface: Grave news concerning married siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brothers Grimm collected German folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm are famous as the Brothers Grimm, collectors of fairy tales.

clue.text: Muscle holds back mafia killer

indicators.note: holds means the muscle letters surround the next piece

parts.note: ab is short for an abdominal muscle

indicators.note: back means the mafia word is turned round

parts.note: the mob is the mafia

explanation.surface: A muscleman protects a mafia hitman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the mafia word and 'holds' puts it in the abdominal muscle; 'killer' is a weapon, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb is a weapon of mass slaughter, hence a killer.

clue.text: Shape being mature, zip coming undone

indicators.note: a zip coming undone falls apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mature figure whose zip is coming undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming undone' rearranges MATURE and ZIP; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapezium is a four-sided geometric figure with one pair of parallel sides.

clue.text: Club gets tennis champion further

parts.note: Chris Evert won eighteen Grand Slam singles titles
on means further, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A club signs a tennis champion to go further.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: Dowdy female having only half the sex?

indicators.note: only half means the second part of the phrase for sex is dropped

parts.note: rumpy-pumpy is jokey British slang for sex

explanation.surface: A frumpy woman who gets only half her share of love-making?
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps RUMPY from rumpy-pumpy, a jokey British term for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpy describes someone dressed in a drab, old-fashioned, unattractive way.
